why: A (riemDist: ℝ≥0∞-valued infimum of pathLength over piecewise smooth paths in N; riemDist_le_pathLength and riemDist_triangle at universe 0 for ANY subset N ⊆ V): riemDist ≤ pathLength, triangle inequality, points outside the normal ball of radius s are at distance ≥ s, and for slice submanifolds riemDist p q = 0 ⇒ p = q. B: for a CONNECTED abstract Riemannian manifold, any two points are joined by a piecewise smooth path and the real-valued ρ (sInf of arcLen) is a metric (≥ 0, ρ = 0 ↔ p = q, symmetric, triangle). A ⇒ B fails genuinely: A concerns subsets of an inner-product space with the ambient norm; an abstract Riemannian manifold is not given as such (Whitney does not preserve the metric, Nash isometric embedding is not available), and B's existence of joining paths in a connected manifold is not in A. B ⇒ A fails: B does not specialize to N ⊆ V without identifying ↥N's induced RiemannianBundle and B's arcLen of paths in ↥N with pathLength in V (missing bridge); A's triangle inequality and ≤ pathLength hold for arbitrary N (no manifold), and A allows disconnected N (riemDist = ⊤), where B's real ρ and ConnectedSpace do not apply; A has no symmetry claim.
